title: The Old Bachelor's Nightcap

full_text:
In a narrow street in Copenhagen lived an old bachelor clerk named Anton. He wore a faded woolen nightcap and spent his quiet life selling pepper and nutmeg in a small shop. The neighbors called him a cold, dried-up recluse who had never known human feeling.

Yet when Anton fell into his final sleep and they lifted the old woolen nightcap from his brow, a worn portrait was discovered beneath the lining, depicting a lovely maiden with golden curls from his native German town.

As a youth, Anton had loved her with his whole soul. He had toiled for decades in foreign lands to earn enough gold to marry her, only to learn on the eve of his return that she had died of a sudden fever, whispering his name. Anton had locked his grief in his breast, preserved her portrait near his brow, and spent his lifetime helping poor apprentices in secret.

The gossiping town had seen only a dusty nightcap; but angels looked upon a crown of lifelong fidelity and sorrow, escorting Anton's soul to a joyful reunion in heaven.
moral: Behind the plainest, most solitary life often rests a sacred sanctuary of faithful, unspoken love.
